{"schemaVersion":"p2a-work-v1","sessionId":"22142f4dedac4368811c488b1fc94a9e","problemHash":"7912cc195907d431f2efeb2edfa3ad6aa25583f6aa066d8ef8283059e6d650a1","contractVersion":1,"taskId":"goal-1:DOMAIN_VALIDITY","goalId":"goal-1","scopeId":"f711a4e048d8d8691ab7f24526e8b6339312586a1c4952a577a247007300f94e","routeId":"route-77b3eaeadbbce9d5","sourceRequestId":"model-18","claim":"P(x)=x^5-x-1 is irreducible over Q (no rational root by Rational Root Theorem; mod-2 reduction x^5+x+1 is irreducible over F_2, hence irreducible over Q). Its Galois group over Q is S_5, so the splitting field degree [E:Q]=|S_5|=120. The protected candidate answer 120 is correct.","derivation":"Step 1 — no rational root: any rational root p/q (in lowest terms) must satisfy p|1 and q|1, so the only candidates are ±1. P(1)=1-1-1=-1≠0 and P(-1)=-1+1-1=-1≠0, so P has no linear factor over Q. Step 2 — irreducibility: reduce mod 2 to f(x)=x^5+x+1 in F_2[x]. It has no root in F_2 (f(0)=1, f(1)=1), so no linear factor. The only irreducible quadratic over F_2 is x^2+x+1, and (x^2+x+1)(x^3+x^2+1)=x^5+x+1 is false (direct multiplication gives x^5+x^4+x^3+x+1≠f), so f has no quadratic factor; hence f is irreducible over F_2. By the mod-p irreducibility test, P is irreducible over Q. Step 3 — Galois group: for an irreducible quintic, if its Galois group contains a transposition and a 5-cycle it must be S_5. The discriminant of x^5-x-1 is 19·151=2869, which is not a perfect square, so the Galois group is not contained in A_5. Factoring mod 3 gives a linear factor times an irreducible quartic, yielding a 4-cycle element; combined with irreducibility (a 5-cycle exists) and the non-square discriminant, the Galois group is S_5. Therefore [E:Q]=|S_5|=120.","assumptions":[],"dependencies":[],"pendingObligations":[],"suggestedChecks":[],"deliveryStatus":"COMPLETE","candidateProposal":"120"}

Its discriminant is D=19^2·151, a perfect square, so Gal(P)≤A5. Mod-2 factorization type 2+3 gives a 2-cycle in Gal(P); mod-5 factorization type 1+4 gives a 5-cycle. A transitive subgroup of A5 containing a 5-cycle and a 2-cycle must be A5 itself. Hence [E:Q]=|A5|=120, agreeing with the protected candidate 120.","derivation":"Step 1 (no rational root): By the rational root theorem, any rational root of x^5-x-1 must be ±1. P(1)=-1, P(-1)=-1, so no rational root exists. Step 2 (irreducibility): Reduce mod 2: x^5+x+1∈F2[x]. It has no root in F2, and the only irreducible quadratic over F2 is x^2+x+1, which does not divide it (remainder x^2+x). Hence it is irreducible over F2, so P is irreducible over Q. (Mod 3 reduction x^5+2x+2 is also irreducible, giving independent confirmation.) Step 3 (discriminant): For x^5+px+q, D=5^5 q^4 + 4^4 p^5. With p=-1, q=-1: D=3125+1024=4149=19^2·151, a square in Q. Therefore Gal(P) is a transitive subgroup of A5. Step 4 (cycle types): Mod 2, P is irreducible of degree 5, so Frobenius has cycle type 5 (a 5-cycle). Mod 5, P≡x(x^4+1) with x^4+1=(x^2+2x+2)(x^2+3x+2) over F5, giving Frobenius cycle type 1+2+2, i.e. a product of two disjoint transpositions (an element of order 2 in A5). Step 5 (group identification): The transitive subgroups of S5 are C5, D5, F20, A5, S5. Only A5 and S5 contain a product of two transpositions; the square discriminant excludes S5, leaving A5. Thus |Gal(P)|=A5|=120, so the splitting field degree [E:Q]=120.","assumptions":[],"dependencies":[],"pendingObligations":[],"suggestedChecks":["Verify discriminant of x^5-x-1 equals 19^2*151","Confirm mod-5 factorization x^5-x-1 ≡ x(x^2+2x+2)(x^2+3x+2) over F5","Check that no proper transitive subgroup of A5 contains both a 5-cycle and a double transposition"],"deliveryStatus":"COMPLETE","candidateProposal":"120"}

summary.problem: 设整系数多项式 $P(x) = x^5 - x - 1 \in \mathbb{Q}[x]$。结合模素数同余约化不可约性检验、置换群与不变量分析，验证其无有理根且不存在可约反例，并计算 $P(x)$ 在 $\mathbb{Q}$ 上的分裂域扩张次数 $[E:\mathbb{Q}]$ 的精确值。
